unreg:extreme_play_length.rederivation_notes: Own chain (written before reading the record): LONGESTFG 70+ = P(season max of MADE regular-season FGs >= 70): count of 65+ attempts (end-of-half/game kick-vs-Hail-Mary policy, fair-catch-kick chances) x kicker leg ceiling (top-tail kickers; preseason and practice evidence) x conditions (altitude Denver/any Mexico City game, dome, wind, temperature, ball-prep rules) with a steeply convex make curve, then an absorbing path state (running max, games left). LONGESTPLAY 99+: offensive gain of 99 needs a snap from own 1 (exposure from punts downed at 1, goal-line stands, penalties) x breakaway conversion, minus penalty-nullified plays; key hazard: does 'play from scrimmage' include interception/fumble/blocked-or-missed-FG returns, which can be 99-109 yards? LONGESTTD/SHORTESTTD title-only. After comparing: the author matches my exposure x conversion decomposition and the absorbing-state logic, and correctly quotes both rules texts (both quotes verified verbatim). Differences: the author asserts as settled that returns are excluded and that a scrimmage play cannot exceed 99 yards; the author omits the current record (68 yd, Cam Little, end of first half, indoors, 2 Nov 2025) and Little's 70-yd preseason make as ceiling evidence; the kicker leg proxy uses kickoff touchback depth, which is confounded by the 2024+ dynamic-kickoff rules; and rule-regime changes (2025 kicking-ball preparation, kickoff rules) are mentioned only generically.

findings.text: The record treats an inference as settled contract text. rules_evidence 'establishes' says the play is 'from scrimmage (not a return)', and variants_and_edge_cases says 'A scrimmage play cannot exceed 99 yards, so the 99+ strike is exactly "a 99-yard play occurs" and requires a snap from the offence's own 1-yard line'. The sampled text only says 'a play from scrimmage of at least 99 yards' and 'officially recorded stats by the Source Agencies'. Interception returns, fumble returns and blocked or missed-FG returns all happen on plays from scrimmage, and they can run 99-109 yards. They also happen far more often than 99-yard offensive gains. Whether they count is CONTRACT_AMBIGUOUS, but no unresolved entry says so. Under the return-inclusive reading the required inputs change: a defensive/return TD length tail and the opponent red-zone INT/fumble rate, with exposure not limited to own-1 snaps. As it stands, nfl.own_one_yard_line_snap_rate is wrongly called a hard bound ('P(YES) is bounded by this rate').
findings.resolution: RESOLVED: valid; rules text ('a play from scrimmage of at least 99 yards') does not exclude returns. Rewrote the KXNFLLONGESTPLAY establishes line and variants, removed the 'bounded' claim from own-1 why/mechanism, added new input nfl.scrimmage_turnover_return_long_tail (stage s1, coverage, required_data), a regime-switch interaction between the two readings, and unresolved u5 (CONTRACT_AMBIGUOUS).

findings.text: The ceiling evidence is incomplete, and the leg proxy is regime-confounded. nfl.kicker_ceiling_range_tail estimates range from 'kickoff hang-adjusted distance (mean yards past the goal line on non-touchbacks, share of touchbacks into the back of the end zone)'. Under the 2024+ dynamic-kickoff rules, and the later change that moves touchbacks to the 35, kick depth is a strategic choice, so it no longer measures leg power cleanly. The record also never states the current regular-season record (68 yd, Cam Little, Nov 2025, end of first half, indoors; the previous record was Tucker's 66). It ignores preseason long makes (Little made a 70-yd preseason kick in 2025), which are out of settlement scope but are the only direct evidence of a 70-yd ceiling. Required data should include preseason/practice long-kick logs and a kickoff-rule era flag.
findings.resolution: RESOLVED: valid. nfl.kicker_ceiling_range_tail rationale/measurement now state the 68-yd 2025 regular-season record, use kickoff depth only as a pre-2024 prior, add an era fixed effect and preseason makes; new input nfl.preseason_long_kick_evidence; kickoff_rule_regime added as era flag; kicker dataset gains era, preseason and record-list fields.

findings.text: Rule-regime changes that shift the 70+ FG rate are missing as inputs. Two examples: the 2025 change on kicking-ball preparation, followed by a record number of 60+ yard makes, and the fair-catch free kick (scored as a field goal, with no rush). u4 only says 'rule shifts (kickoff regime, punting strategy)' and does not apply this to the field-goal contract. A pre-2025 tail fit ('all regular-season plays since 1999') will understate the current long-kick rate unless an era term is added.
findings.resolution: RESOLVED: valid. Added new input nfl.kicking_ball_and_fg_rule_era (2025 K-ball preparation, fair-catch free kick, kickoff regime) to stage s3 and officiating coverage; play_length_evt_tail_fit measurement now carries a pre-2024/2024/2025+ era term; unresolved u7 records the small post-2025 sample and u2 the fair-catch-kick counting question.

findings.text: The roles of the as-of state are mislabelled. nfl.season_to_date_pace (running maximum and games left) is KEEP_CONTEXT, yet it is an absorbing state: once a qualifying event happens the market is decided, and the author's own saturating interaction depends on it. It should be primary. nfl.long_fg_attempt_and_make_model is primary but appears in no mechanism stage. So does nfl.kicker.
findings.resolution: RESOLVED: valid. nfl.season_to_date_pace audit changed to KEEP_PRIMARY and catalog_entry role to primary (absorbing state); nfl.long_fg_attempt_and_make_model and nfl.kicker added to stage s3 input_ids.

findings.text: nfl.endzone_exposure_plays (KEEP_SECONDARY) largely duplicates nfl.own_one_yard_line_snap_rate under the offensive-only reading; the record should mark it DUPLICATE_OF or say what extra signal it adds. situational_schedule_motivation is NOT_APPLICABLE, yet a 70-yd kick is a historic milestone. Record-chasing attempts in low-stakes end-of-half moments, especially indoors (as Little's 68 was), are a plausible situational effect. The venue x weather interaction text 'in domes only for the altitude-free case' is garbled.
findings.resolution: RESOLVED: valid. nfl.endzone_exposure_plays audited DUPLICATE_OF:nfl.own_one_yard_line_snap_rate, removed from stage s1 and pace_volume coverage, role set to context; situational_schedule_motivation now COVERED via a record-chase covariate in the attempt hazard; garbled venue x weather interaction text rewritten.

findings.text: td_play_length_by_source says the shortest TD 'is 1 yard in effectively every season'. Zero-yard touchdowns (a fumble recovered in the end zone) exist, so the minimum can be 0. If KXNFLSHORTESTTD turns out to be a per-game window, it is not near-certain. This is acknowledged in u1 only as a window question.
findings.resolution: RESOLVED: valid. Rules text now shows KXNFLSHORTESTTD/LONGESTTD are single-game inclusive buckets with zero-TD = NO; td_play_length_by_source rationale now notes 0-yard recovery TDs; new stage s6 and input nfl.game_td_length_order_stats model per-game max/min with the zero-TD mass.

unreg:nfl_draft_selection.rederivation_notes: Own chain (written before reading the record): draft order (standings plus SOS tiebreak, then playoff exit round; 32 = Super Bowl winner; forfeits) -> pick ownership and trades (pre-draft and draft night) -> prospect pool (underclass declaration deadline in January, the three-years-out-of-high-school eligibility clock, NCAA eligibility rulings, return-to-school incentives now that NIL/revenue-sharing pay exists, medicals at the combine) -> team boards (QB need, consensus board, GM habits, regime change after Black Monday, top-30 visits) -> sequential order statistics (3rd QB, top 5) -> settlement (league position label, team that makes the pick). Supplemental draft: whether it is held, the petition ruling, and a bid that costs the next-year pick in the same round. Rounds 2-7 and compensatory picks matter for the last-pick and team-by-round series. All four quotes checked verbatim. After comparing: the author's five-stage chain matches mine on order, trades, eligibility, team choice and labelling, and the round-1 order rules are correct (19-24 WC losers, 25-28 divisional, 29-30 conference, 31/32). Differences: the order engine and history are limited to round one; the declaration gate omits the eligibility clock and NIL-era return incentives; the record does not cover a Supplemental Draft that is not held; and some claims go beyond the rules text.

findings.text: The mechanism is scoped to round one while several series are not. nfl.draft_order_rules_engine maps results to 'overall slots 1-32 of round one'. required_data history is '2000-2026 drafts for the top 32', and nfl.gm_draft_behavior_history uses 'rounds 1-2'. Yet the archetype contains KXNFLLASTPICKPOS (the last pick of the draft is a round-7 compensatory slot), KXNFLDRAFTEAMPOS ('Will team draft a position across round') and the position-drafted series (RB/TE/LB/OL/DB/EDGE), which can resolve in later rounds. Required inputs and data are missing: compensatory-pick allocation (announced in March), the full seven-round order and ownership, and a slot-dispersion model and consensus boards beyond the top 32-100, where public boards are thin.
findings.resolution: RESOLVED: valid. Added new input nfl.full_draft_order_compensatory_picks (seven rounds, March compensatory release, final selection) and stage s7 for last-pick/team-round series; slot dispersion and GM behaviour measurements extended to all rounds; draft history required data now 2000-2026 all rounds; u10 records thin late-round boards.

findings.text: The declaration and eligibility gate is mis-measured, though it is the dominant factor in November for KXNFLDRAFTPICK (Austin Simmons) and KXNFLDRAFTQB/TOP (Trinidad Chambliss). The measurement uses 'class, projected round (first-round projected prospects declare at about 95 percent...)' over 'the 5 most recent draft classes'. It omits the league eligibility rule (three seasons removed from high school), which is binding for early enrollees and reclassified prospects. It also omits NCAA eligibility rulings and litigation (extra-year waivers) and the NIL/revenue-sharing era change in return-to-school incentives, which is strongest for QBs. The '95 percent' figure is unsourced, and a pre-NIL base rate will be biased. Required inputs: eligibility clock per prospect, NCAA eligibility case status, and an NIL-era declare-rate indicator.
findings.resolution: RESOLVED: valid. Removed the unsourced 95 percent declare rate; declaration measurement now uses post-2021 (NIL-era) early-entry lists; new input nfl.prospect_eligibility_clock_and_nil_era (three-years-from-high-school clock, NCAA waiver/litigation status, NIL flag) added to stage s1, availability and officiating coverage, and required data.

findings.text: Settlement claims go beyond the rules text. The 'establishes' line for the KXNFLDRAFTPICK quote says 'if he is not drafted or goes elsewhere the market resolves NO', and variants say a non-declaring player 'resolves NO'. The text only states the YES condition. Draft postponement or cancellation is unaddressed, and for KXNFLSDRAFTTOP the case where no Supplemental Draft is held (rules_secondary is empty) is not listed in unresolved. These should be marked as inferences or CONTRACT_AMBIGUOUS.
findings.resolution: RESOLVED: valid. KXNFLDRAFTPICK establishes line now marks the NO case as inference; KXNFLDRAFTTEAM quote added as the only explicit undrafted=NO text; variants rewritten; unresolved u7 (undrafted/non-declare and neither-matchup-player cases) and u8 (draft postponement, Supplemental Draft not held) added.

findings.text: There are duplicate and mislabelled inputs. nfl.standings_sim is KEEP_SECONDARY while its own reason says it 'partly duplicates the season simulation' (nfl.season_sim_distribution); it should be DUPLICATE_OF or have its role split. nfl.insider_report_conversion is KEEP_CONTEXT, yet draft-week and draft-night insider reports are the main late information for exact-slot markets that stay open into the draft. Its reason, that it applies 'for availability events rather than picks', contradicts its own why text. nfl.offfield_base_rate, nfl.roster_continuity and nfl.event_calendar_hazard are in catalog_entry but in no stage. gm_draft_behavior_history has category 'matchup'.
findings.resolution: RESOLVED: valid. standings_sim reason/why rewritten to its distinct tiebreak role (season_sim supplies win counts); insider_report_conversion changed to KEEP_SECONDARY with consistent reason and role; roster_continuity added to s3, event_calendar_hazard and offfield_base_rate (now WEAK) to s1; gm_draft_behavior_history category changed to other.

findings.text: Consensus boards and mock drafts (nfl.draft_board, nfl.prospect_slot_dispersion_model) increasingly anchor on sportsbook draft odds near the draft. The record says nothing about this contamination, so a market-derived signal can enter through the consensus input. The record should require vintages that exclude odds-driven mocks, or flag the contamination in unresolved.
findings.resolution: RESOLVED: valid. Slot dispersion measurement and the consensus-board dataset timestamp rule now exclude mocks/boards citing sportsbook odds; draft_board audit reason notes the contamination; unresolved u6 (SOURCE_UNVERIFIED) records that no archive tags odds-informed boards.

findings.text: Some figures are unverified. The trade-hazard prior of 'about 30 percent for picks 1-10' and the Supplemental Draft 'weighted-lottery order based on previous season records' (in fact a tiered lottery: teams grouped by record/playoff status) are stated without a source. Treat them as SOURCE_UNVERIFIED.
findings.resolution: RESOLVED: valid. Removed the 30 percent top-10 trade prior from the trade-graph measurement (now an estimated slot-band rate); Supplemental Draft mechanism relabelled as a lottery within record-based tiers; unresolved u9 (SOURCE_UNVERIFIED) asks for a trade-log computation and the league procedures document.

unreg:super_bowl_mvp.rederivation_notes: Own chain (written before reading the record): P(player) = sum over finalist pairs of P(team reaches and wins the Super Bowl) x P(MVP | win). The team layer needs a season and playoff bracket simulation, a neutral-site rating with full-strength lineups, and QB status. The game layer needs the in-game production distribution (QB passing/rushing, skill-player yards and TDs, defensive splash plays, return TDs) conditioned on script. The vote layer: a media panel (about 80%) plus a fan vote (about 20%), with ballots cast before the final whistle, a QB premium of roughly half of winners, a one-time losing-team winner (SB V) and one co-MVP (SB XII). Hazards: all series TITLE_ONLY; co-MVP handling, position classification of two-way or hybrid players and returners, a ticker/title conflict (KXNFLSBMVPQB titled 'Non QB'), and whether the markets trade in-game. After comparing: the author's three-layer decomposition, the winner-only renormalisation, the defender regime switch and the exclusion of market inputs (blueprint m.quote_history/m.external_lines dropped, market-free rating used) all match mine. Differences: no lifecycle or in-game state, settlement_contract marked COVERED despite no rules, and the ballot timing is treated only as unresolved.

findings.text: The market lifecycle and live state are missing. Super Bowl MVP markets typically keep trading during the game until the announcement, and ballots are cast before the end (fan voting closes in the 4th quarter). The record lists no m.lifecycle input, no live score/box-score state input and no live play-by-play dataset; all required_data timestamps are 'before kickoff'. Because the series are TITLE_ONLY, close time is unknown. This should be disclosed as CONTRACT_AMBIGUOUS, and if the markets trade in-game, a live in-game feed and a running-leader-at-ballot-time input are required.
findings.resolution: RESOLVED: valid. Added m.lifecycle (audited KEEP_SECONDARY) and new input nfl.sb_mvp_live_ballot_state with stage s6, a regime-switch interaction and a live-feed/lifecycle required_data entry; s5 notes fan voting closes in the fourth quarter; close time recorded as CONTRACT_AMBIGUOUS u6.

findings.text: category_coverage settlement_contract is 'COVERED' by m.rules_text and m.settlement_truth, but no series has rules text (rules_verification NOT_VERIFIED_NO_RULES_TEXT). The honest status is GAP, tied to u1.
findings.resolution: RESOLVED: finding was correct when written; rules text now exists for KXNFLSBMVP and KXNFLSBMVPPOS (quoted, rules_verification PARTIALLY_VERIFIED), so settlement_contract stays COVERED by m.rules_text plus the new depth-chart position map, with DEF/QB variants and close time held in u1/u5/u6.

findings.text: The ticker/title conflict is not noted. KXNFLSBMVPQB is titled 'Non QB Championship MVP', but its suffix suggests a QB-YES contract. The author assumes the non-QB reading without flagging that YES could be the complement. Settlement direction should be in unresolved.

nfl.sb_mvp_historical_position_base_rates is 'secondary', yet the author calls it 'the only data for position and non-QB contracts'. For KXNFLSBMVPPOS/KXNFLSBMVPQB it is effectively the primary prior. Also, the bye adjustment says '+0.5 points for a bye-week team in the semifinal only', but the bye applies in the divisional round (after the wild-card round), so the text is confused. nfl.news is in catalog_entry but in no stage.
findings.resolution: RESOLVED: valid. sb_mvp_historical_position_base_rates role set to primary in new_inputs and catalog_entry; bye text replaced (no rest term in the final; bye effect only on reaching it via the divisional round); nfl.news added to stage s2.

findings.text: Historical box scores for pre-1982 finals lack official sacks (and tackles are unofficial throughout), so the conditional-credit logit 'on all Super Bowls since 1967' with sack covariates relies on incomplete or unofficial fields. This is SOURCE_UNVERIFIED for PFR coverage of those fields.
findings.resolution: RESOLVED: valid. Conditional-credit measurement now uses sacks only for 1982+ games with a missing indicator and drops tackles as unofficial; PFR coverage of these fields recorded as SOURCE_UNVERIFIED unresolved u7.
